label: sparse: early original-phase step after x/l/s bigram, or first copy step re-inputting j (no clean rule)
explanation: Very sparse feature (0.03% of steps, about 1.7k dev sequences) with a narrow magnitude range (median 0.12, max 0.19). It has two loose loci. (1) Original phase, mostly t=3-4: steps right after the prefix tokens x, l, s (or w) when x/l/w/v came two steps back, e.g. d x l [s], f c x l [q]. (2) First copy step (recall_idx 1, the input after <DEL> is orig(0)) when the first token is j or d, stronger for long sequences. It almost never fires at t<2, at the delimiter step, or once copying has gone wrong. Both clauses have very low precision (2-5%): the same contexts usually leave the feature off, so it seems to depend on some specific hidden-state conjunction that no predicate built from these variables captures. The best disjunction has F1 about 0.06 and mass recall about 0.53 on dev.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: phase=2 & in_tok=j (+5.87), prev_tok=x (+4.19), recall_idx=1 (+4.11), orig0=d (+3.68), prev_tok=s (+3.57), prev2_tok=x (+3.35). Lower it: orig_idx=-1 (-3.45), orig2=i (-2.66), orig1=b (-2.44), orig0=l (-2.34).
